name: Centro Documental de la Memoria Histórica, Salamanca
story: In 1937–38 the Nationalists set up a documents office in Salamanca to gather papers seized from Republican parties, unions, Masonic lodges and individuals — raw material for the repression, especially under the 1940 Law for the Repression of Freemasonry and Communism. The archive later became the General Archive of the Civil War, and in 2007 the Centro Documental de la Memoria Histórica. Its holdings now serve historians and relatives of victims of both sides. Catalan government papers held here were returned to Catalonia from 2006 after a long political dispute (the 'papeles de Salamanca').
see: A permanent exhibition including a reconstructed Masonic lodge room made from confiscated regalia and material on the documentation service; reading room for researchers.
plan: Exhibition free, usually weekday mornings and some afternoons — check the Ministry of Culture site; photo ID required for the reading room.

boxes.text: The return of the 'Salamanca papers' to Catalonia was politically contested in Salamanca and in court.
